# Exodra — LLM reference

Exodra is a schema-first, fine-grained UI runtime with **no virtual DOM** and no
scheduler. Read this before writing any Exodra code; almost every mistake comes
from assuming React (or from an older Exodra that no longer exists — see the last
section).

This file is hand-written and short. For the complete generated documentation, see
**[llms-full.txt](https://exodra.org/llms-full.txt)**.

## The one idea: a component is a SCHEMA plus a MACHINE

- a **schema** — the shape, built **once when the module loads**, with named
  **ports**: places a value may be put later;
- a **machine** — the behaviour of one instance: initial state, transitions that
  write ports, event handlers, and effects that follow outside data.

Nothing is diffed and nothing is walked at render time. A schema is compiled once
per backend into a prototype, a walk plan and a writer per port; a render clones the
prototype and runs the machine. The *same* machine runs on the server, on a client
render and through hydration.

```ts
import {
    EXO_PORT_EVENT,
    EXO_PORT_TEXT,
    composeExoMachine,
    createExoMachine,
    createExoSchema,
    exoPorts,
    withExoHandlers,
    withExoTransitions,
    withExoWire,
} from '@exodra/core';
import type { TExoMachineNodeOf } from '@exodra/core';
import { ExoDomBackend, withExoCompiler } from '@exodra/dom';
import type { TExoDomNode } from '@exodra/dom';

const CounterPorts = exoPorts({ COUNT: EXO_PORT_TEXT, INCREMENT: EXO_PORT_EVENT });

const CounterSchema = createExoSchema(CounterPorts, (b) => {
    b.el('div', { class: 'counter' }, (div) => {
        div.el('span', null, (span) => span.textPort(CounterPorts.COUNT));
        div.el('button', { class: 'btn', type: 'button' }, (button) => {
            button.eventPort(CounterPorts.INCREMENT, 'click');
            button.text('Increment');
        });
    });
});

const counterBase = createExoMachine(CounterSchema, {
    createInitialState: (c: TExoDomNode) => ({ n: 0 }),
});

function showCount(c: TExoMachineNodeOf<typeof counterBase>): void {
    c.text(CounterPorts.COUNT, c.state.n);
}

export const counterMachine = composeExoMachine(
    counterBase,
    (m) => withExoTransitions(m, {
        increment: (c) => {
            c.state.n += 1;
            showCount(c);
        },
    }),
    (m) => withExoWire(m, (c) => showCount(c)),
    (m) => withExoHandlers(m, (on) => on(CounterPorts.INCREMENT, (c) => increment(c))),
);
export const { increment } = counterMachine.transitions;

const backend = withExoCompiler(new ExoDomBackend());
const dispose = backend.render(counterMachine, document.body);
```

**Schema emitter** (`b`): `el(tag, attrs?, fn?)` and `text(value)` declare what
never changes; `attrPort(port, name)`, `textPort(port)`, `eventPort(port, name)`,
`refPort(port)` and `childrenPort(port)` put a port declared in `exoPorts` at a
**place**.

**Machine** — `createExoMachine(schema, { createInitialState })`, then decorators
composed with `composeExoMachine(base, ...steps)`; each step returns a new machine:

- `createInitialState: (c, params) => state` runs **once** per instance and
  **returns the state**. It is also where children ports are opened
  (`c.childList`, `c.one`, `c.list`, `c.keyedList`).
- `withExoTransitions(m, { name: (c, …args) => … })` — a dictionary of transitions;
  the machine exposes them as `machine.transitions.name` and swaps them with
  `machine.overrides({ name: alt })`. Code the machine only calls itself is a plain
  function over `TExoMachineNodeOf<typeof base>`.
- `withExoWire(m, (c, params) => …)` writes ports from params; it re-runs through
  `wireExoNode(node, machine, params)`.
- `withExoHandlers(m, (on) => on(port, (c, event) => …))` — event handlers.
- `withExoEffects(m, (effect) => effect((c) => unsubscribe | null))` — follows
  outside data while the instance is live.

**Exonode** (`c`): `text(port, v)`, `attr(port, v)`, `unsafeHtml(port, markup)`,
`state`, `provide` / `inject`, `onTeardown(fn)`, and the children calls below.

## Data reaches ports through transitions and effects

There is no reactive-value package, no `.value`, no `bind`. Outside data is followed
by an **effect** that draws first, then subscribes, and returns the unsubscribe:

```ts no-check
function show(c: TExoMachineNodeOf<typeof labelBase>): void {
    c.text(LabelPorts.LABEL, store.getValue());
}
export const labelMachine = composeExoMachine(
    labelBase,
    (m) => withExoEffects(m, (effect) => {
        effect((c) => {
            show(c);
            return store.onChange(() => show(c));
        });
    }),
);
```

`store` is whatever your data layer is — an `@oimdb/*` collection
(`OIMEffectService.INSTANCE.subscribeEffect(db, () => show(c), slots)`) or any
object with a subscription. The first `show(c)` must be synchronous inside the
effect: hydration adopts server rows only while the instance is being armed.

App state that belongs to one instance is machine state (`c.state.x`), changed by
handlers and transitions.

## Children ports

A children port renders exactly where `childrenPort()` was called, so it can stand
**between static siblings** with no wrapper.

| Call | What stands there | Changes later? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `c.one(port, machine, params)` | one instance | no |
| `c.list(port, machine, rows)` | one instance per entry, `rows[i]` as its params | no |
| `c.childList(port)` | a placed-children handle you drive yourself | yes |
| `c.keyedList(port, keyOf, build, update)` | a keyed list (plugin) | yes |

`c.build(machine, params)` returns a complete, wired, detached child.

## Lists and identity

`reconcileExoOrder(kids, shown, keys, want, build)` from `@exodra/list-reconcile`
reconciles **by identity**: the same key as before keeps its DOM node, a new key is
built, a missing key is removed. Pass the items themselves as `keys` and identity
is the item reference:

```ts no-check
const listBase = createExoMachine(ListSchema, {
    createInitialState: (c: TExoDomNode) => ({
        rows: c.childList(ListPorts.ROWS),
        shown: [] as TItem[],
    }),
});
function showRows(c: TExoMachineNodeOf<typeof listBase>): void {
    const want = items.getValue();
    c.state.shown = reconcileExoOrder(c.state.rows, c.state.shown, want, want, (item) =>
        c.build(rowMachine, item)
    );
}
export const listMachine = composeExoMachine(
    listBase,
    (m) => withExoEffects(m, (effect) => {
        effect((c) => {
            showRows(c);
            return items.onChange(() => showRows(c));
        });
    }),
);
```

**So a row keeps its DOM node, its focus and its scroll position only if you hand
back the same object.** That is a fact about your data layer, not about the
renderer.

**Keys are a plugin, never a core default.** Compose `EXO_KEYED_LIST_VOCABULARY`
onto the backend (`composeExoPlugins(backend, EXO_KEYED_LIST_VOCABULARY)`) and call
`c.keyedList(port, keyOf, build, update)` in `createInitialState`; it returns
`{ reconcile(items) }` — keep it in state and call it from a transition. A surviving
key keeps its row, and `update(row, item)` runs only when the object under the key
changed. The free-function form is `createExoKeyedList(kids, keyOf, build, update)`.

## Events

`withExoHandlers(m, (on) => on(port, handler))`. How a listener reaches the DOM is the backend's `events`
field: `EXO_DIRECT_EVENTS` (one listener per element) is the default;
`createExoDelegatedEvents(names, options?)` attaches one root listener per event
name. Compose it with
`composeExoPlugins(backend, { events: () => createExoDelegatedEvents(['click']) })`.
Delegation refuses non-bubbling events unconditionally and high-frequency ones
unless `{ allowHighFrequency: true }`.

## Contexts

`c.provide(token, value)` / `c.inject(token)` on the exonode; the token is
`exoContextToken<T>('name')` from `@exodra/context`. A context is not reactive by
itself: put an object with a subscription in it and follow it with an effect.

## SSR and hydration

`renderExoPage(machine, { params, state, head, status })` from `@exodra/ssr` renders
on the string backend and returns `{ html, status, headers, head, stateScript,
state, renderDocument() }`. During the render a machine reaches the response with
`c.inject(EXO_SSR_RESPONSE)` — `setStatus`, `setHeader`, `addHead`,
`setState(key, value)`. On the client, `readExoStateScript()` returns that state.

Hydration is a pack: `withExoHydration(withExoCompiler(new ExoDomBackend()))`, then
`backend.hydrate(machine, container, params?)`. The container is the element whose
first element child the server rendered.

## Escape hatches

- `exoForeignNode(c, element, hooks?)` gives a hand-built element the half a child
  needs, so a list can place, move and drop it. Client render only.
- `exoNodeDom(child)` reaches a child's DOM record.
- `c.onTeardown(fn)` registers a teardown against the instance.
- `c.unsafeHtml(childrenPort, html)` writes raw markup. Nothing escapes and nothing
  sanitises.

## JSX (optional — and it DOES need a compiler)

JSX declares a **schema** and nothing else: markup plus named ports.
`exoJsx<TPorts>(($) => <markup/>)` from `@exodra/jsx` is compiled by
`@exodra/babel-plugin-schema` (or `swc-plugin-exodra` in Rust) into a module-level
`createExoNamedSchema()` call; the value is a schema declaration whose `.ports` are
named. It emits imports from `@exodra/core` only. There is **no runtime**: JSX that
reaches the runtime uncompiled throws, and there is no `Fragment`. There are no props
and no wire in a declaration — the machine (`createExoMachine(Schema)` plus its decorators)
fills the ports.

| Written | Compiles to | Filled by the machine with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `class="row"`, `tabindex={0}`, `disabled` | markup folded into the schema | — |
| `data-id={$.id}` | `port('data-id', 'id')` | `c.attr(P.id, v)` |
| `<b>{$.label}</b>` (the element's ONLY child) | `textPort('label')` | `c.text(P.label, v)` |
| `onClick={$.toggle}`, `on:dblclick={$.edit}` | `eventPort('click', 'toggle')` — `onX` lowers the tail, `on:` keeps the name | `on(P.toggle, handler)` in `withExoHandlers` |
| `ref={$.box}` | `refPort('box')` | — |
| `unsafeHtml={$.body}` | `childrenPort('body')` | `c.unsafeHtml(P.body, html)` — nothing escapes |
| `<$.rows />` | `childrenPort('rows')`, may stand among static siblings | `c.one` / `c.list` / `c.childList` + `reconcileExoOrder` |

```tsx
import { exoJsx } from '@exodra/jsx';
import { composeExoMachine, createExoMachine, withExoHandlers, withExoWire } from '@exodra/core';
import type { TExoEventPort, TExoMachineNode, TExoMachineNodeOf, TExoTextPort } from '@exodra/core';

const CounterSchema = exoJsx<{ count: TExoTextPort; increment: TExoEventPort }>(($) => (
  <button type="button" onClick={$.increment}>
    <span>{$.count}</span>
  </button>
));
const P = CounterSchema.ports;

const counterBase = createExoMachine(CounterSchema, {
  createInitialState: (c: TExoMachineNode) => ({ n: 0 }),
});

function showCount(c: TExoMachineNodeOf<typeof counterBase>): void {
  c.text(P.count, c.state.n);
}

export const counterMachine = composeExoMachine(
  counterBase,
  (m) => withExoWire(m, (c) => showCount(c)),
  (m) => withExoHandlers(m, (on) => on(P.increment, (c) => {
    c.state.n += 1;
    showCount(c);
  })),
);
```

Refused at compile time, each naming the element and the fix: any expression other
than `$.name` (closures, `item.id`, conditionals); component tags (`<Row />`) and any
`list=` / `props=` operand; fragments; `{...spread}`; a namespace other than `on:`; a
lowercase inline handler (`onclick="…"`); a text port beside other children;
`unsafeHtml` with children; a port name used twice; JSX outside `exoJsx()`; statements
before the declaration's `return`.

Setup: `npm i @exodra/jsx`, `npm i -D babel-preset-exodra`,
`module.exports = { presets: ['exodra'] }`, and `"jsx": "react-jsx"` +
`"jsxImportSource": "@exodra/jsx/schema"` in tsconfig. Options (preset and plugin):
`schemaSource` (default `'@exodra/core'`), `schemaImport` (default
`'createExoNamedSchema'`), `markerName` (default `'exoJsx'`).
The native TypeScript JSX transform and `@babel/plugin-transform-react-jsx` are
**incompatible** — they emit `jsx()` runtime calls and Exodra has no runtime to
receive them.

## Packages

- `@exodra/core` — schemas, ports, the machine (`createExoMachine`,
  `composeExoMachine`, `withExoTransitions`, `withExoWire`, `withExoHandlers`,
  `withExoEffects`, `wireExoNode`), `createExoStatic`, `composeExoPlugins`, the shared escapers.
- `@exodra/context` — `exoContextToken`, context frames, ids.
- `@exodra/computed` — the declarative machine form (`withExoComputedMachine`).
- `@exodra/dom` — the browser backend: `ExoDomBackend`, `withExoCompiler`,
  `withExoHydration`, event packs, `exoForeignNode`.
- `@exodra/list-reconcile` — `reconcileExoOrder`, `createExoKeyedList`,
  `EXO_KEYED_LIST_VOCABULARY`.
- `@exodra/string` — the server backend: `ExoStrBackend`.
- `@exodra/ssr` — the rest of the response: `renderExoPage`, `EXO_SSR_RESPONSE`,
  `readExoStateScript`.
- `@exodra/jsx` — the JSX schema dialect.
- `@exodra/babel-plugin-schema` — the JSX compiler. `babel-preset-exodra` wires it
  in one line; `esbuild-plugin-exodra`, `rollup-plugin-exodra`, `bun-plugin-exodra`
  and `@exodra/vite-plugin` delegate to the same runner; `swc-plugin-exodra` is the
  Rust/Wasm equivalent for SWC.
- `@exodra/router` — `createExoRouter`, `provideExoRouter`, `exoOutlet`, `ExoLink`,
  history adapters, guards; a page receives its match as its wire's params.
- `@exodra/forms` — `readExoControlValue` and friends.
- `@exodra/dom-profiler`, `@exodra/introspect` — profiling, and ESLint rules plus a
  source counter.
- `@exodra/react`, `@exodra/react-mount`, `@exodra/react-compat` — React interop.
- `create-exodra` — `npm create exodra` scaffolding.

## Gotchas

1. **`createInitialState` returns state and opens children ports; it does not write
   ports.** Writing happens in transitions, called from `wire`, handlers and effects.
2. **An effect draws before it subscribes.** Subscribing alone leaves the port empty
   until the first change.
3. **Identity is upstream.** Focus loss in an editable list is a data-layer
   problem: hand back the same object, or use the keyed-list plugin.
4. **A children port cannot be followed by static text** — the schema compiler
   refuses this at module load. Wrap the text.
5. **Inside a raw-text element** (`<script>`, `<style>`, …) a `textPort()` is
   refused, a child *element* is refused, and static text is emitted verbatim.
6. **A machine that calls `exoNodeDom` or `exoForeignNode` is a client machine.**
   `@exodra/string` has no element.

## What does NOT exist (delete this from your priors)

- `@exodra/reactivity` / `@exodra/reactivity-types`: `exoBindable`, `exoDerive`,
  `exoList`, `exoCombine`, `exoPersist`, persistors, `bindExoText` / `bindExoAttr`
  / `bindExoHtml`. Use machine state, transitions and effects.
- `c.bind`, `c.set`, `bindList`, `bindOne`, `bindMany`, `bindChildren`,
  `reconcileExoChildren`, `reconcileExoKeyedChildren`, `attachExoKeyedList`.
- `exoComponent`, `exoSchema`, `exoStatic`, `exoOne`, `renderExoRows`,
  `hydrateExoRows`, `exoOwn`, `exoRuntime` / `exoDefaultRuntime`, `EXO_SSR`.
- `h(type, attrs)` / `defineComponent(fn)` / prop buckets (`static`, `bindable`,
  `handlers`, …).
- `@exodra/babel-plugin-jsx`, `babel-plugin-exodra-jsx`, a `key` prop in JSX.
